clue.text: Regularly keen, therefore I am full of this, ultimately?

definitions.text: Regularly keen, therefore I am full of this, ultimately?

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word keen, here the second and fourth

parts.note: therefore means thus

indicators.note: full of says the phrase therefore I am holds another piece within it
ultimately points to the very last letter of the word this

explanation.surface: A playful twist on Descartes: being keen, I think, therefore I am brimming with this feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone keen and full of 'this' is full of eagerness, playing on Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness that fills a person is eager zeal, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Gag not beginning to make a deep impression

indicators.note: not beginning says the first letter of the synonym for gag is dropped

parts.note: to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A comedian's joke that fails to start yet still leaves a lasting mark on the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but is the verb meaning to heave; 'not beginning' drops the R of RETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave by cutting into a surface with acid leaves a deep mark, so the phrase is a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Great Dane barking — one provides food and drink

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of Great Dane go wild

explanation.surface: A large dog barks at someone serving refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' fits the dog but is the anagram signal; 'barking' (mad) is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor cafe garden serving tea and refreshments is a place providing food and drink.

clue.text: Item about France being out of shape

indicators.note: about says one piece wraps around another

parts.note: an item is a single unit
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A news item about France losing its form.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of shape is in poor physical condition, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Monkey I'm with that is eating rubbish

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: eating says the abbreviation for that is takes in another piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone eating junk food in the company of a friend who copies them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' looks like a noun but is the verb, to copy; TAT is British for tasteless junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To monkey someone is to ape or copy them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Nicer pudding taken to the Queen

parts.note: in Britain a sweet is a pudding or dessert
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A dessert brought to the monarch, which is the more pleasant thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more pleasant is more agreeable, a comparative synonym.

clue.text: Bird's caught — frown when head and tail are removed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.text: when head and tail are removed
indicators.note: head and tail removed means the word frown loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bird is trapped and looks displeased once beheaded and docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook-like black bird of the genus Corvus is a familiar example of a bird.

clue.text: Rushed ruddy sandwiches roughly over

indicators.note: sandwiches says the colour word holds another piece between its letters

parts.note: ruddy means red

indicators.note: over says the abbreviation for roughly is turned around

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: A red-faced person hurriedly makes sandwiches and gets it done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruddy' may suggest a mild British oath, but it means red; 'over' turns CA into AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hurried at speed is to have dashed, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: New dress I ordered around west end of Lambeth — a desolate place

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap another piece
ordered means the letters of new dress I are put in a different arrangement
the west end of a word written across a map is its left end, its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman orders a new dress from somewhere in west London's Lambeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west end' suggests London's West End, but means the leftmost letter of Lambeth, L, which goes inside the anagram of NEW DRESS I. Lambeth is a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninhabited, barren wasteland is a bleak and empty place.

clue.text: After church, get a very loud teasing

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces follow the abbreviation for church

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: After the church service, someone gets a loud ribbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-hearted banter is good-natured mockery, so it is teasing as a noun.

clue.text: I make a mark in one car's front — and a learner's the same

parts.note: to dent something is to make a mark in it
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: front picks the first letter of car's

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain

explanation.surface: A driver confesses to scratching the front of a learner's car, and the learner did likewise.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things exactly alike are indistinguishable, which is meant by the same.

clue.text: To reversing taxi, starts to call out: 'Put that in your pipe and smoke it!'

definitions.text: Put that in your pipe and smoke it!

indicators.note: reversing says the word for taxi is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of call and out

explanation.surface: Someone reversing a taxi shouts a defiant retort at a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom of defiance: taken literally, what goes in a pipe to be smoked is this leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured leaf packed into a bowl and lit is literally what one puts in a pipe to smoke.

clue.text: Pull at belt

parts.note: a belt of land is a tract, an area or zone

explanation.surface: A tug at someone's belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' suggests clothing but means a stretch of land, as in a green belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something toward oneself is to exert a pull on it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Seal — a nocturnal animal? Not right

indicators.note: not right says the R, the abbreviation for right, is removed

parts.note: a badger is a nocturnal animal

explanation.surface: Is a seal really a night-time creature? That seems wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' tempts as the marine animal alongside 'nocturnal animal', but it is an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem or insignia pressed or worn as a mark of office is a seal in the heraldic sense.

clue.text: Pedant admitting awful editor must be indulged

indicators.note: admitting says the word for pedant lets another piece inside

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous pedant
awful means vile

explanation.surface: A fussy pedant must humour a dreadful editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pampered with special advantages has been favoured and spoilt.

clue.text: Drunk diner — we blame this?

indicators.note: drunk says the letters of diner and we are scrambled as if tipsy

explanation.surface: A tipsy diner, and we know which beverage to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: what a drunk diner might blame for the state they are in.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass of claret or merlot is what a dinner guest might blame for getting tipsy.

clue.text: Genuine criminal's innocent

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of genuine are treated badly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine criminal claims innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innocent' is a noun here, an innocent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive young woman, especially as a stage role, is an innocent.

clue.text: A cricket club involved in run out with no backing up — one's got black eyes!

indicators.note: involved in says the letters for A cricket club sit inside run out

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is short for out

indicators.note: backing up says the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: A cricket match where a run-out with no support leaves a player with black eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black eyes' suggests a fight, but the animal has a black mask around its eyes. A run-out is a way of dismissing a batter in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A masked North American mammal has dark fur around each eye, so it has black eyes.

clue.text: Arranged to search to save miner, finally — one could be in the pit

definitions.text: one could be in the pit

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe, here held inside the rearranged letters
arranged means the letters of to search are put in a new order
finally picks the last letter of miner

explanation.surface: A search is arranged to rescue a trapped miner from the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The mining picture is a decoy: the pit is the orchestra pit below a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's band of musicians plays in the sunken area in front of the stage.

clue.text: Very fine female lost rag over sauce

indicators.note: lost says the abbreviation for female drops out of fine
over says the word rag is turned around

explanation.surface: A very fine woman loses her rag about a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost rag' reads as a temper tantrum (British 'lose your rag'), but 'lost' removes F from FINE and 'over' turns RAG into GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour condiment is sprinkled on chips like a dressing, a loose example of sauce.

clue.text: Usual way to squeeze in

indicators.note: to squeeze says the word for way presses around another piece

parts.note: a route is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: The normal way to squeeze in somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and habitual is the standard, customary thing, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Picks clubs and hearts over diamonds and spades

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
H is the card abbreviation for hearts
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ice is slang for diamonds
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player picks from the four suits.
explanation.walkthrough: The suits lure the solver into card abbreviations, but 'over' is cricket's O and diamonds become ICE, slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Selections or options someone has taken are their picks, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Conservative girl in charge? Excellent

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Tory woman takes charge, and it's terrific.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the highest quality and lasting worth, an adjective synonym for first-rate.

clue.text: Portion of salade nicoise, piled high

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heaped helping of the classic French tuna salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavily loaded or burdened, as a plate stacked to the top, is an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Fish — 55 found in river

indicators.note: found in says the numeral sits inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
LV is 55 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fifty-five fish discovered in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is the verb, to search or rummage, not a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish around for something is to dig or search into it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A battle to get a French female to come round, unconscious

indicators.note: to come round says the French article wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a
a war is a battle

explanation.surface: After a battle, a Frenchwoman comes round from unconsciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come round' suggests waking from a faint, but it is the container signal; 'a French female' is the feminine article.
explanation.definitionFit: Not knowing or not conscious of something, the adjective sense of being oblivious.

clue.text: A profit — not for the first time!

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Making a profit, and not for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more means it is repeated, so it is not the first occasion.

clue.text: Amount of land in far corner, oddly cropped

indicators.note: oddly cropped says the odd-placed letters of far corner are cut away, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A plot of land in a far corner, strangely harvested.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of area of 4,840 square yards measures a quantity of ground.

clue.text: Eli struggling with Elgar's long passages

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of Eli and Elgar's thrash about into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A musician named Eli battles with Elgar's lengthy passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long passages' suggests stretches of music, but means corridors or covered walkways.
explanation.definitionFit: Long covered walkways or corridors, as in a stately home, are elongated passages.

clue.text: Volunteers knocked back by temperature — one cold room!

indicators.note: knocked back says the abbreviation for the volunteers is turned around

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Volunteers are turned away because of the temperature in one chilly room.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A space under the roof of a house is one kind of room.

clue.text: Outstanding first bit of tart — a piece for two

parts.note: an outstanding bill is due, still to be paid

indicators.note: first bit of picks the opening letter of tart

explanation.surface: An excellent first slice of tart, shared between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise but means owing; 'a piece for two' sounds like dessert but is music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition for two performers is a piece for a pair.

clue.text: Share 'er American money with young servant outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for young servant goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a page is a young servant
taken as written, the dropped-h form of her
a cent is a unit of American money

explanation.surface: Giving her a cut of the American cash, with a young servant standing by.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion of a whole is someone's cut or portion, a noun synonym.
